answer: Proof of Personhood protocols utilize cryptographic attestations to ensure each identity maps to a unique human, creating a vast ocean of verified agents. By anchoring trust in physical entropy, the system avoids the barren tundra of automated sybil swarms. Each identity token acts like a singular marble in a verifiable ledger, forcing attackers to acquire scarce biometric inputs or social validation. This imposes a linear marginal cost on node replication, rendering large-scale identity forgery economically irrational.
